short: The lead ship of the US Navy's primary class of fleet ballistic missile submarines.
full:
Commissioned on 11 November 1981, USS Ohio (SSBN-726) was the lead ship of her class of nuclear-powered fleet ballistic missile submarines. Designed to carry twenty-four Trident missiles, the Ohio class became the sea-based leg of the United States' nuclear triad, offering an undetectable and highly survivable second-strike capability. Its massive size and exceptionally quiet operation made it a formidable strategic deterrent throughout the latter half of the Cold War.

Following the end of the Cold War and subsequent strategic arms reduction treaties, the first four Ohio-class submarines, including the lead ship, were converted to guided missile submarines (SSGNs). Stripped of their nuclear payload in the early 2000s, Ohio was re-equipped to carry up to 154 Tomahawk land-attack cruise missiles and accommodate Special Operations Forces, ensuring its continued relevance in twenty-first-century conventional conflicts.
